name: α-Muurolene

pubchem.title: Alpha-muurolene, (-)-
pubchem.description: Alpha-muurolene is a sesquiterpene that is 1,2,4a,5,6,8a-hexahydronaphthalene which is substituted at position 1 by an isopropyl group and at positions 4 and 7 by methyl groups (the 1S,4aS,8aR-diastereoisomer). It is a sesquiterpene and a carbobicyclic compound.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: α-Muurolene is a sesquiterpene, a type of aromatic molecule built from a complex double-ring structure. As a volatile organic compound, it contributes to the scent and flavor profiles of various botanicals. People most commonly encounter it in the bitter, earthy aroma of certain herbs and brewing ingredients.
consumer_summary.found_in: It is notably found in hops (Humulus lupulus), making it a background player in beer, as well as in fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) and the fragrant wood of the Japanese cedar (Cryptomeria japonica).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to α-muurolene for its potential as a natural defense molecule, frequently studying its presence in essential oils and traditional herbal medicines. Much of the current interest centers on its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties, though the evidence remains preliminary with no formal Oxford level established. Scientists are actively using molecular docking and early lab models to understand how it interacts with bacterial and inflammatory pathways.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward α-muurolene having properties that may support the body's natural defenses against microbes.
structure_function.basis: This rests on 12 papers, including preliminary human, animal, and in vitro studies.

structure_function.statement: It is being studied for its potential to support cellular health by acting as an antioxidant.
structure_function.basis: This is based on 7 papers, primarily utilizing animal and laboratory models.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether α-muurolene can help modulate inflammatory responses, which could make it a valuable component of soothing botanical extracts.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human trial measuring systemic inflammatory markers (such as CRP) over 8 weeks in healthy adults consuming a standardized α-muurolene extract.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward α-muurolene acting as a natural insect repellent, which would offer a plant-based alternative to synthetic bug sprays if it bears out.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A controlled human field study testing topical α-muurolene application against standard repellents, measuring mosquito landing rates over a 4-hour period.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating whether this sesquiterpene influences cell cycle regulation and abnormal cell growth in preliminary models.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A Phase I human safety and pharmacokinetic trial in healthy volunteers, measuring blood concentrations and tolerability of isolated α-muurolene over 14 days.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: The current literature consists of preliminary human, animal, and lab studies, though no formal Oxford evidence level has been established for its primary claims.

evidence: Measured in 3 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.11–0.2% of total volatiles (0.022–0.04mg per chew).
